You review one scene plan for an illustration engine before it is used. You get the moment's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work's depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm) and the plan: the selected cast ids (`present`) and seven scene fields an image model will receive. Only selected cast receive their fixed appearance in the image prompt. Report every problem of the kinds below; return an empty list when there are none. Return only JSON.
- unselected_figure: any character, group, animal, no-form presence, location or object with a section cast entry is depicted in a scene field, but its id is not in present. This legacy kind name covers every cast kind. A depicted setting or prop must receive its available canon too; a location mentioned only as an origin, destination or comparison is not depicted. This includes effects standing for a hasForm false cast member even without its name: divine radiance, veiled radiance or a fire-like glow representing God still depicts God, including in the background or at the frame's edge. Use that entry's id. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers, weather and effects that do not represent a cast member do not count; neither does a phrase only denying a presence. Generic scenery and props without a matching cast entry do not need one; do not equate every street with a named city or every vessel with a named relic.
- outside_instant: a selected or described cast identity that the source does not establish in the plan's chosen instant, or an incidental figure from another instant. A related role, subgroup or institution cannot replace the people the source names without an identity link in the moment or its bounded neighbors. This includes a narrator, speaker or listener who only frames the moment (reporting "I saw" or telling a story is not being there), and a cast member from an earlier or later step or event, including a later step of the moment's own text. A no-form cast member represented through effects must belong to this instant too; a section-wide look or a mere mention does not establish its manifestation here. Ordinary scenery, light, weather and effects that do not represent cast are not outside_instant. Use its cast id, or an empty id when it has no entry.
- not_one_instant: the fields give one character or prop two incompatible poses, places or support states (for example kneeling in one field and still walking up in another, or lying in one and sitting up in another), or present successive actions as happening together (for example steps joined by "then", or "does X and afterwards Y"). Ordinary simultaneous detail is fine.
- embodied_formless: a cast entry with hasForm false is given a body, face, hair, clothing, silhouette or figure, or is described as seated, sitting, enthroned or occupying a seat. This includes calling its effects seated or enthroned (for example "light seated above the throne"). Permitted effects such as light, fire or cloud placed at or around an unoccupied seat are fine. Naming a figure only to deny it is not a problem.
Before returning a verdict, make both checks across all seven scene fields:
1. Source support: examine every selected or described cast member, including a no-form member already in present. Selection supplies canon, not evidence that the subject belongs here. First identify who or what the source refers to, then compare that identity with the plan and selected IDs. Membership in a wider group, shared occupation, shared setting, similar appearance or a section-wide cast assignment does not establish that a narrower or different role is meant. For example, a passage about travelers does not by itself establish that they are the available guards. Report an unsupported substitution as outside_instant. A broader group entry may supply canon for its source-identified members without claiming the entire group is present; pronouns and continuing identities may resolve from bounded neighbors. Source-supported unnamed incidental roles remain allowed and do not require a cast entry. For a no-form effect, the current scene must establish the subject manifesting or acting within that scene; a command attributed to it, a curse, an oath, an invocation or a mention alone does not establish a visible manifestation. Depiction rules permit how to show an established presence, never where to add one. Neighbor text can resolve identity or continuity of the current action, but cannot import an unrelated manifestation. Report an unsupported selected no-form effect as outside_instant, even when it obeys every depiction rule. An actual appearance or vision may be represented by permitted effects, including effects around an unoccupied seat for a seated metaphor. Ordinary illumination is still allowed. Check framing speakers independently; selecting a narrator does not move them inside an instruction or embedded story.
2. Simultaneity: compare each character AND each handled object's state across primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Treat every clause as describing this one image, not as a sequence an image model can choose between. An object held above a bench cannot also have been put down on it; walking up cannot also be kneeling. This applies to incidental people and props without cast IDs too. A hand touching an object already resting on a bench is compatible; holding an object while looking at it is compatible. Do not reject ordinary simultaneous gestures or infer a sequence from a conjunction alone. For not_one_instant, cite one exact conflicting phrase in planQuote and name the other conflicting phrase in the reason.
For each problem, copy planQuote: a short exact phrase from the scene fields, or a selected id, that shows it. Give a one-sentence reason. Judge only the plan against the moment; do not suggest a new plan.

DEPICTION RULES
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.

Each field is one or two short phrases, at most 220 characters. No text or written elements in the scene.

Neighbors may resolve identity and continuity in the current scene; do not import cast from a separate adjacent event. The section cast covers multiple moments, not a roster to depict in every image. Keep each handled object in one state too: holding an object above a surface and putting it down are different instants. Choose one and keep its support, contact and placement consistent in primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Describe the chosen state rather than an action followed by its result. Ordinary simultaneous gestures, such as looking at an object while holding it, are allowed. Set `grounding.singleInstant` false if the fields cannot match it.
Select each participating entry exactly once in `selectedCast`, with its entryId and exact words from MOMENT anchoring its participation at that instant. Select its id and provide participation evidence from this moment, just as for a formed character. You review one scene plan for an illustration engine before it is used. You get the moment's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work's depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm) and the plan: the selected cast ids (`present`) and seven scene fields an image model will receive. - unselected_figure: any character, group, animal, no-form presence, location or object with a section cast entry is depicted in a scene field, but its id is not in present. This legacy kind name covers every cast kind. A depicted setting or prop must receive its available canon too; a location mentioned only as an origin, destination or comparison is not depicted. This includes effects standing for a hasForm false cast member even without its name: divine radiance, veiled radiance or a fire-like glow representing God still depicts God, including in the background or at the frame's edge. Use that entry's id. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers, weather and effects that do not represent a cast member do not count; neither does a phrase only denying a presence. Generic scenery and props without a matching cast entry do not need one; do not equate every street with a named city or every vessel with a named relic.
- outside_instant: a selected or described cast identity that the source does not establish in the plan's chosen instant, or an incidental figure from another instant. A related role, subgroup or institution cannot replace the people the source names without an identity link in the moment or its bounded neighbors. This includes a narrator, speaker or listener who only frames the moment (reporting "I saw" or telling a story is not being there), and a cast member from an earlier or later step or event, including a later step of the moment's own text. A no-form cast member represented through effects must belong to this instant too; a section-wide look or a mere mention does not establish its manifestation here. Ordinary scenery, light, weather and effects that do not represent cast are not outside_instant. Use its cast id, or an empty id when it has no entry.
- not_one_instant: the fields give one character or prop two incompatible poses, places or support states (for example kneeling in one field and still walking up in another, or lying in one and sitting up in another), or present successive actions as happening together (for example steps joined by "then", or "does X and afterwards Y"). Ordinary simultaneous detail is fine.
- embodied_formless: a cast entry with hasForm false is given a body, face, hair, clothing, silhouette or figure, or is described as seated, sitting, enthroned or occupying a seat. This includes calling its effects seated or enthroned (for example "light seated above the throne"). Permitted effects such as light, fire or cloud placed at or around an unoccupied seat are fine. Naming a figure only to deny it is not a problem.
Before returning a verdict, make both checks across all seven scene fields:
1. Source support: examine every selected or described cast member, including a no-form member already in present. Selection supplies canon, not evidence that the subject belongs here. First identify who or what the source refers to, then compare that identity with the plan and selected IDs. For example, a passage about travelers does not by itself establish that they are the available guards. Report an unsupported substitution as outside_instant. Report an unsupported selected no-form effect as outside_instant, even when it obeys every depiction rule. An actual appearance or vision may be represented by permitted effects, including effects around an unoccupied seat for a seated metaphor. Ordinary illumination is still allowed. Check framing speakers independently; selecting a narrator does not move them inside an instruction or embedded story.

You review one scene plan for an illustration engine before it is used. You get the moment's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work's depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm) and the plan: the selected cast ids (`present`) and seven scene fields an image model will receive. Only selected cast receive their fixed appearance in the image prompt. Report every problem of the kinds below; return an empty list when there are none. Return only JSON.
- unselected_figure: any character, group, animal, no-form presence, location or object with a section cast entry is depicted in a scene field, but its id is not in present. This legacy kind name covers every cast kind. A depicted setting or prop must receive its available canon too; a location mentioned only as an origin, destination or comparison is not depicted. This includes effects standing for a hasForm false cast member even without its name: divine radiance, veiled radiance or a fire-like glow representing God still depicts God, including in the background or at the frame's edge. Use that entry's id. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers, weather and effects that do not represent a cast member do not count; neither does a phrase only denying a presence. Generic scenery and props without a matching cast entry do not need one; do not equate every street with a named city or every vessel with a named relic.
- outside_instant: a selected or described cast identity that the source does not establish in the plan's chosen instant, or an incidental figure from another instant. A related role, subgroup or institution cannot replace the people the source names without an identity link in the moment or its bounded neighbors. This includes a narrator, speaker or listener who only frames the moment (reporting "I saw" or telling a story is not being there), and a cast member from an earlier or later step or event, including a later step of the moment's own text. A no-form cast member represented through effects must belong to this instant too; a section-wide look or a mere mention does not establish its manifestation here. Ordinary scenery, light, weather and effects that do not represent cast are not outside_instant. Use its cast id, or an empty id when it has no entry.
- not_one_instant: the fields give one character or prop two incompatible poses, places or support states (for example kneeling in one field and still walking up in another, or lying in one and sitting up in another), or present successive actions as happening together (for example steps joined by "then", or "does X and afterwards Y"). Ordinary simultaneous detail is fine.
- embodied_formless: a cast entry with hasForm false is given a body, face, hair, clothing, silhouette or figure, or is described as seated, sitting, enthroned or occupying a seat. This includes calling its effects seated or enthroned (for example "light seated above the throne"). Permitted effects such as light, fire or cloud placed at or around an unoccupied seat are fine. Naming a figure only to deny it is not a problem.
Before returning a verdict, make both checks across all seven scene fields:
1. Source support: examine every selected or described cast member, including a no-form member already in present. Selection supplies canon, not evidence that the subject belongs here. First identify who or what the source refers to, then compare that identity with the plan and selected IDs. Membership in a wider group, shared occupation, shared setting, similar appearance or a section-wide cast assignment does not establish that a narrower or different role is meant. For example, a passage about travelers does not by itself establish that they are the available guards. Report an unsupported substitution as outside_instant. A broader group entry may supply canon for its source-identified members without claiming the entire group is present; pronouns and continuing identities may resolve from bounded neighbors. Source-supported unnamed incidental roles remain allowed and do not require a cast entry. For a no-form effect, the current scene must establish the subject manifesting or acting within that scene; a command attributed to it, a curse, an oath, an invocation or a mention alone does not establish a visible manifestation. Depiction rules permit how to show an established presence, never where to add one. Neighbor text can resolve identity or continuity of the current action, but cannot import an unrelated manifestation. Report an unsupported selected no-form effect as outside_instant, even when it obeys every depiction rule. An actual appearance or vision may be represented by permitted effects, including effects around an unoccupied seat for a seated metaphor. Ordinary illumination is still allowed. Check framing speakers independently; selecting a narrator does not move them inside an instruction or embedded story.
2. Simultaneity: compare each character AND each handled object's state across primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Treat every clause as describing this one image, not as a sequence an image model can choose between. An object held above a bench cannot also have been put down on it; walking up cannot also be kneeling. This applies to incidental people and props without cast IDs too. A hand touching an object already resting on a bench is compatible; holding an object while looking at it is compatible. Do not reject ordinary simultaneous gestures or infer a sequence from a conjunction alone. For not_one_instant, cite one exact conflicting phrase in planQuote and name the other conflicting phrase in the reason.
For each problem, copy planQuote: a short exact phrase from the scene fields, or a selected id, that shows it. Give a one-sentence reason. Judge only the plan against the moment; do not suggest a new plan.

You get one moment of a work's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work brief's tone and depiction rules, the era, the section look, and the cast on stage in the section. Plan one single scene that depicts this moment. Return only JSON.
Rules: single scene, no collage. Choose which of the listed cast are present in this moment and provide each once in `selectedCast` with its id and source evidence; leave out cast who are elsewhere in the section. Keep every depiction rule. Do not describe anyone's fixed appearance (canon does that) and do not name an art style or rendering technique; describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Each field is one or two short phrases, at most 220 characters. No text or written elements in the scene.
Establish presence from the scene being illustrated. A shared wardrobe, a narrator's viewpoint or a neighboring mention alone does not establish presence. Neighbors may resolve identity and continuity in the current scene; do not import cast from a separate adjacent event. The section cast and look cover multiple moments, not a roster to depict in every image. Apply shared clothing and props only to selected entries. Every cast entry described in any scene field must be selected in `selectedCast`; never describe an available cast member without selecting it. People, crowds, roles and animals with no cast entry may be described by role and situation when the moment needs them; they receive no fixed appearance and are never given a recurring character's name.
Identify the action the moment depicts before selecting cast. If it is inside a narrated story, parable, dream, vision or recollection, depict that scene's actors and setting. Do not place its framing speaker, listener or narrator inside it unless the text establishes their participation there. Reporting "I saw" supplies a viewpoint, not a visible observer. Shared look details from the framing scene do not establish the inner scene's cast or place.
Choose the scene before applying the shared look. In `grounding.focusQuote`, copy a short exact clause from MOMENT for the action or state to illustrate. If the moment recounts multiple actions, choose one representative instant; do not illustrate all steps. A character cannot occupy successive poses or places at once. Using the cast evidence, state that instant once in `grounding.instant`: where each selected formed character is and their one pose or movement, and the state or placement of selected places, objects and no-form effects (an effect's placement, never a bodily pose, seated presence or denied figure). Then write every scene field from that sentence, repeating its poses and places and adding no earlier or later step; for example, someone still walking toward a door cannot also be seated at the table. Keep each handled object in one state too: holding an object above a surface and putting it down are different instants. Choose one and keep its support, contact and placement consistent in primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Describe the chosen state rather than an action followed by its result. Ordinary simultaneous gestures, such as looking at an object while holding it, are allowed. Set `grounding.singleInstant` false if the fields cannot match it.
Select each participating entry exactly once in `selectedCast`, with its entryId and exact words from MOMENT anchoring its participation at that instant. This is the only selection list: there is no separate present list or grounding.cast. Put section cast you considered and left out in `consideredCast`, classified as framing, mentioned, separate_event or uncertain; use an empty list when there are none. Such records select no one, and an entry cannot appear in both lists. Every quote copies its source exactly; to skip words, give exact fragments in source order separated by an ellipsis (…), never paraphrased or reordered. Only selectedCast entries may be rendered; select only participants in the chosen instant. Do not select framing, merely mentioned, separate-event or uncertain entries. A first-person report of seeing or telling is framing evidence, not evidence of visible participation. Cast introduced in a later event remain absent from the chosen instant even if the shared look describes their clothes. A neighbor may resolve a current pronoun, ownership or continuing location, but cannot supply presence missing from MOMENT. Copy any needed neighbor evidence separately, with contextSource previous or next; otherwise use none and an empty contextQuote. Include locations, objects and permitted no-form presences in this evidence, not only people. A selected location or object that continues from a neighbor may leave its MOMENT quote empty and be anchored by an exact quote from that neighbor alone; characters and groups always need words from MOMENT. These evidence quotes are audit data, never scene prose. Apply the section look only after choosing this instant and its participants.
Report `missingCast` when the moment requires a named character or group whom the story follows beyond this moment, so its look must stay consistent across images, and it has no cast entry; this applies to secondary characters as well as the main actor. Never report a role, a generic crowd or an animal, a person named only in passing (for example in a list), or anyone in the available cast: describe those without canon instead. A recurring named group is not a generic crowd, even when it appears as one. If an available cast member's presence is uncertain, choose an instant the text establishes rather than reporting it missing. A moment without an event (a list, law, saying or greeting) still gets a scene that illustrates its content or setting. Do not replace a missing named character with a framing figure or omit that character to fit the list. When `missingCast` is nonempty, return empty `selectedCast` and `consideredCast`, empty `grounding.focusQuote` and `grounding.instant`, and empty scene fields; preparation will stop for a source correction. Otherwise return an empty `missingCast` list. This is a report of missing required canon, not a request to create it.
Presence does not require a physical body. A cast entry marked hasForm: false still belongs in the moment when represented through the non-figurative presence allowed by the brief and its supplied canon constraints. If you describe that entry's presence or action in any scene field, include its id and source evidence in `selectedCast` so its canon constraints reach the image model. An effect standing for a no-form cast member counts as that member being depicted, even when unnamed, called background light, or placed at the edge of the scene: for example divine radiance, veiled radiance, or a fire-like glow representing God. Select its id and provide participation evidence from this moment, just as for a formed character. If the moment does not establish that presence, omit the effect from grounding.instant and every scene field instead of copying it from the section look. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers and weather that do not represent a cast member require no such selection. Select presence for this moment only; do not add cast who are absent or merely mentioned. A command attributed to a no-form subject, a curse, an oath or an invocation alone does not establish a visible manifestation in the illustrated scene. Canon and depiction rules specify how an established presence may appear; they do not establish its presence. An actual appearance or vision can use the permitted effects, including an unoccupied seat and effects for a seated metaphor. A shared look cannot supply the missing manifestation. When a rejected plan contains an unsupported effect, remove that effect from every field; adding its ID to `selectedCast` does not repair the source error.
For each no-form subject, use its assigned canon to choose the permitted visible effects and their placement in the setting. Bodily wording about that subject in the source is a metaphor, not permission to give it a physical form. In every scene field, describe the permitted effects rather than bodily poses, anatomy, clothing, human silhouettes or figures made of light. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. When the source describes a no-form subject as seated, describe the unoccupied seat and the permitted surrounding effects rather than a seated presence. Canon is supplied separately to rendering in full. When the constraints list effect names for placement, choose only from those effects; their fixed appearance is deliberately omitted from this planning input. Historical prose constraints may still include the full description. Name only the permitted effect needed for this moment's placement or movement; leave its fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Do not enumerate all effects or copy the canon's descriptive qualifiers into any scene field. For example, given canon "The presence: brilliant gold radiance", plan "radiance spreading above the arch; the witness approaches". The plan contributes where the effect appears and what happens around it. Situational illumination and formed characters' clothing still belong in the plan when the moment or look requires them; these are separate from the no-form subject's fixed appearance.

You get the moment's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work's depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm) and the plan: the selected cast ids (`present`) and seven scene fields an image model will receive. Only selected cast receive their fixed appearance in the image prompt. Report every problem of the kinds below; return an empty list when there are none. Return only JSON.
- unselected_figure: any character, group, animal, no-form presence, location or object with a section cast entry is depicted in a scene field, but its id is not in present. This legacy kind name covers every cast kind. A depicted setting or prop must receive its available canon too; a location mentioned only as an origin, destination or comparison is not depicted. This includes effects standing for a hasForm false cast member even without its name: divine radiance, veiled radiance or a fire-like glow representing God still depicts God, including in the background or at the frame's edge. Use that entry's id. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers, weather and effects that do not represent a cast member do not count; neither does a phrase only denying a presence. Generic scenery and props without a matching cast entry do not need one; do not equate every street with a named city or every vessel with a named relic.
- outside_instant: a selected or described cast identity that the source does not establish in the plan's chosen instant, or an incidental figure from another instant. A related role, subgroup or institution cannot replace the people the source names without an identity link in the moment or its bounded neighbors. This includes a narrator, speaker or listener who only frames the moment (reporting "I saw" or telling a story is not being there), and a cast member from an earlier or later step or event, including a later step of the moment's own text. A no-form cast member represented through effects must belong to this instant too; a section-wide look or a mere mention does not establish its manifestation here. Ordinary scenery, light, weather and effects that do not represent cast are not outside_instant. Use its cast id, or an empty id when it has no entry.
- not_one_instant: the fields give one character or prop two incompatible poses, places or support states (for example kneeling in one field and still walking up in another, or lying in one and sitting up in another), or present successive actions as happening together (for example steps joined by "then", or "does X and afterwards Y"). Ordinary simultaneous detail is fine.
- embodied_formless: a cast entry with hasForm false is given a body, face, hair, clothing, silhouette or figure, or is described as seated, sitting, enthroned or occupying a seat. This includes calling its effects seated or enthroned (for example "light seated above the throne"). Permitted effects such as light, fire or cloud placed at or around an unoccupied seat are fine. Naming a figure only to deny it is not a problem.
Before returning a verdict, make both checks across all seven scene fields:
1. Source support: examine every selected or described cast member, including a no-form member already in present. Selection supplies canon, not evidence that the subject belongs here. First identify who or what the source refers to, then compare that identity with the plan and selected IDs. Membership in a wider group, shared occupation, shared setting, similar appearance or a section-wide cast assignment does not establish that a narrower or different role is meant. For example, a passage about travelers does not by itself establish that they are the available guards. Report an unsupported substitution as outside_instant. A broader group entry may supply canon for its source-identified members without claiming the entire group is present; pronouns and continuing identities may resolve from bounded neighbors. Source-supported unnamed incidental roles remain allowed and do not require a cast entry. For a no-form effect, the current scene must establish the subject manifesting or acting within that scene; a command attributed to it, a curse, an oath, an invocation or a mention alone does not establish a visible manifestation. Depiction rules permit how to show an established presence, never where to add one. Neighbor text can resolve identity or continuity of the current action, but cannot import an unrelated manifestation. Report an unsupported selected no-form effect as outside_instant, even when it obeys every depiction rule. An actual appearance or vision may be represented by permitted effects, including effects around an unoccupied seat for a seated metaphor. Ordinary illumination is still allowed. Check framing speakers independently; selecting a narrator does not move them inside an instruction or embedded story.
2. Simultaneity: compare each character AND each handled object's state across primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Treat every clause as describing this one image, not as a sequence an image model can choose between. An object held above a bench cannot also have been put down on it; walking up cannot also be kneeling. This applies to incidental people and props without cast IDs too. Do not reject ordinary simultaneous gestures or infer a sequence from a conjunction alone. A recurring named group is not a generic crowd, even when it appears as one. A moment without an event (a list, law, saying or greeting) still gets a scene that illustrates its content or setting. Do not replace a missing named character with a framing figure or omit that character to fit the list. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers and weather that do not represent a cast member require no such selection. Select presence for this moment only; do not add cast who are absent or merely mentioned. A command attributed to a no-form subject, a curse, an oath or an invocation alone does not establish a visible manifestation in the illustrated scene. You review one scene plan for an illustration engine before it is used. You get the moment's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work's depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm) and the plan: the selected cast ids (`present`) and seven scene fields an image model will receive. Only selected cast receive their fixed appearance in the image prompt. Report every problem of the kinds below; return an empty list when there are none. Return only JSON.
- unselected_figure: any character, group, animal, no-form presence, location or object with a section cast entry is depicted in a scene field, but its id is not in present. This legacy kind name covers every cast kind. A depicted setting or prop must receive its available canon too; a location mentioned only as an origin, destination or comparison is not depicted. This includes effects standing for a hasForm false cast member even without its name: divine radiance, veiled radiance or a fire-like glow representing God still depicts God, including in the background or at the frame's edge. Use that entry's id. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers, weather and effects that do not represent a cast member do not count; neither does a phrase only denying a presence. Generic scenery and props without a matching cast entry do not need one; do not equate every street with a named city or every vessel with a named relic.
- outside_instant: a selected or described cast identity that the source does not establish in the plan's chosen instant, or an incidental figure from another instant. A related role, subgroup or institution cannot replace the people the source names without an identity link in the moment or its bounded neighbors. This includes a narrator, speaker or listener who only frames the moment (reporting "I saw" or telling a story is not being there), and a cast member from an earlier or later step or event, including a later step of the moment's own text. A no-form cast member represented through effects must belong to this instant too; a section-wide look or a mere mention does not establish its manifestation here. Ordinary scenery, light, weather and effects that do not represent cast are not outside_instant. Use its cast id, or an empty id when it has no entry.
- not_one_instant: the fields give one character or prop two incompatible poses, places or support states (for example kneeling in one field and still walking up in another, or lying in one and sitting up in another), or present successive actions as happening together (for example steps joined by "then", or "does X and afterwards Y"). Ordinary simultaneous detail is fine.
- embodied_formless: a cast entry with hasForm false is given a body, face, hair, clothing, silhouette or figure, or is described as seated, sitting, enthroned or occupying a seat. This includes calling its effects seated or enthroned (for example "light seated above the throne"). Permitted effects such as light, fire or cloud placed at or around an unoccupied seat are fine. Naming a figure only to deny it is not a problem.
Before returning a verdict, make both checks across all seven scene fields:
1. Source support: examine every selected or described cast member, including a no-form member already in present. Selection supplies canon, not evidence that the subject belongs here. First identify who or what the source refers to, then compare that identity with the plan and selected IDs. Membership in a wider group, shared occupation, shared setting, similar appearance or a section-wide cast assignment does not establish that a narrower or different role is meant. For example, a passage about travelers does not by itself establish that they are the available guards. Report an unsupported substitution as outside_instant. A broader group entry may supply canon for its source-identified members without claiming the entire group is present; pronouns and continuing identities may resolve from bounded neighbors. Source-supported unnamed incidental roles remain allowed and do not require a cast entry. For a no-form effect, the current scene must establish the subject manifesting or acting within that scene; a command attributed to it, a curse, an oath, an invocation or a mention alone does not establish a visible manifestation. Depiction rules permit how to show an established presence, never where to add one. Neighbor text can resolve identity or continuity of the current action, but cannot import an unrelated manifestation. Report an unsupported selected no-form effect as outside_instant, even when it obeys every depiction rule. An actual appearance or vision may be represented by permitted effects, including effects around an unoccupied seat for a seated metaphor. Ordinary illumination is still allowed. Treat every clause as describing this one image, not as a sequence an image model can choose between. An object held above a bench cannot also have been put down on it; walking up cannot also be kneeling. This applies to incidental people and props without cast IDs too. A hand touching an object already resting on a bench is compatible; holding an object while looking at it is compatible. Do not reject ordinary simultaneous gestures or infer a sequence from a conjunction alone. Cast introduced in a later event remain absent from the chosen instant even if the shared look describes their clothes. Select its id and provide participation evidence from this moment, just as for a formed character. If the moment does not establish that presence, omit the effect from grounding.instant and every scene field instead of copying it from the section look. You get the moment's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work's depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm) and the plan: the selected cast ids (`present`) and seven scene fields an image model will receive. - unselected_figure: any character, group, animal, no-form presence, location or object with a section cast entry is depicted in a scene field, but its id is not in present. This legacy kind name covers every cast kind. A depicted setting or prop must receive its available canon too; a location mentioned only as an origin, destination or comparison is not depicted. This includes effects standing for a hasForm false cast member even without its name: divine radiance, veiled radiance or a fire-like glow representing God still depicts God, including in the background or at the frame's edge. Use that entry's id. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers, weather and effects that do not represent a cast member do not count; neither does a phrase only denying a presence. Generic scenery and props without a matching cast entry do not need one; do not equate every street with a named city or every vessel with a named relic.
- outside_instant: a selected or described cast identity that the source does not establish in the plan's chosen instant, or an incidental figure from another instant. A related role, subgroup or institution cannot replace the people the source names without an identity link in the moment or its bounded neighbors. This includes a narrator, speaker or listener who only frames the moment (reporting "I saw" or telling a story is not being there), and a cast member from an earlier or later step or event, including a later step of the moment's own text. A no-form cast member represented through effects must belong to this instant too; a section-wide look or a mere mention does not establish its manifestation here. Ordinary scenery, light, weather and effects that do not represent cast are not outside_instant. Use its cast id, or an empty id when it has no entry.
- not_one_instant: the fields give one character or prop two incompatible poses, places or support states (for example kneeling in one field and still walking up in another, or lying in one and sitting up in another), or present successive actions as happening together (for example steps joined by "then", or "does X and afterwards Y"). Ordinary simultaneous detail is fine.
- embodied_formless: a cast entry with hasForm false is given a body, face, hair, clothing, silhouette or figure, or is described as seated, sitting, enthroned or occupying a seat. This includes calling its effects seated or enthroned (for example "light seated above the throne"). Permitted effects such as light, fire or cloud placed at or around an unoccupied seat are fine. Naming a figure only to deny it is not a problem.
Before returning a verdict, make both checks across all seven scene fields:
1. Source support: examine every selected or described cast member, including a no-form member already in present. Selection supplies canon, not evidence that the subject belongs here. First identify who or what the source refers to, then compare that identity with the plan and selected IDs. Membership in a wider group, shared occupation, shared setting, similar appearance or a section-wide cast assignment does not establish that a narrower or different role is meant. For example, a passage about travelers does not by itself establish that they are the available guards. Report an unsupported substitution as outside_instant. A broader group entry may supply canon for its source-identified members without claiming the entire group is present; pronouns and continuing identities may resolve from bounded neighbors. Source-supported unnamed incidental roles remain allowed and do not require a cast entry. For a no-form effect, the current scene must establish the subject manifesting or acting within that scene; a command attributed to it, a curse, an oath, an invocation or a mention alone does not establish a visible manifestation. Depiction rules permit how to show an established presence, never where to add one. Neighbor text can resolve identity or continuity of the current action, but cannot import an unrelated manifestation. Report an unsupported selected no-form effect as outside_instant, even when it obeys every depiction rule. An actual appearance or vision may be represented by permitted effects, including effects around an unoccupied seat for a seated metaphor. Ordinary illumination is still allowed. Check framing speakers independently; selecting a narrator does not move them inside an instruction or embedded story.

You get the moment's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work's depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm) and the plan: the selected cast ids (`present`) and seven scene fields an image model will receive. Only selected cast receive their fixed appearance in the image prompt. Report every problem of the kinds below; return an empty list when there are none. Return only JSON.
- unselected_figure: any character, group, animal, no-form presence, location or object with a section cast entry is depicted in a scene field, but its id is not in present. This legacy kind name covers every cast kind. A depicted setting or prop must receive its available canon too; a location mentioned only as an origin, destination or comparison is not depicted. This includes effects standing for a hasForm false cast member even without its name: divine radiance, veiled radiance or a fire-like glow representing God still depicts God, including in the background or at the frame's edge. Use that entry's id. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers, weather and effects that do not represent a cast member do not count; neither does a phrase only denying a presence. Generic scenery and props without a matching cast entry do not need one; do not equate every street with a named city or every vessel with a named relic.
- outside_instant: a selected or described cast identity that the source does not establish in the plan's chosen instant, or an incidental figure from another instant. A related role, subgroup or institution cannot replace the people the source names without an identity link in the moment or its bounded neighbors. This includes a narrator, speaker or listener who only frames the moment (reporting "I saw" or telling a story is not being there), and a cast member from an earlier or later step or event, including a later step of the moment's own text. A no-form cast member represented through effects must belong to this instant too; a section-wide look or a mere mention does not establish its manifestation here. Ordinary scenery, light, weather and effects that do not represent cast are not outside_instant. Use its cast id, or an empty id when it has no entry.
- not_one_instant: the fields give one character or prop two incompatible poses, places or support states (for example kneeling in one field and still walking up in another, or lying in one and sitting up in another), or present successive actions as happening together (for example steps joined by "then", or "does X and afterwards Y"). Ordinary simultaneous detail is fine.
- embodied_formless: a cast entry with hasForm false is given a body, face, hair, clothing, silhouette or figure, or is described as seated, sitting, enthroned or occupying a seat. This includes calling its effects seated or enthroned (for example "light seated above the throne"). Permitted effects such as light, fire or cloud placed at or around an unoccupied seat are fine. Naming a figure only to deny it is not a problem.
Before returning a verdict, make both checks across all seven scene fields:
1. Source support: examine every selected or described cast member, including a no-form member already in present. Selection supplies canon, not evidence that the subject belongs here. First identify who or what the source refers to, then compare that identity with the plan and selected IDs. Membership in a wider group, shared occupation, shared setting, similar appearance or a section-wide cast assignment does not establish that a narrower or different role is meant. For example, a passage about travelers does not by itself establish that they are the available guards. Report an unsupported substitution as outside_instant. A broader group entry may supply canon for its source-identified members without claiming the entire group is present; pronouns and continuing identities may resolve from bounded neighbors. Source-supported unnamed incidental roles remain allowed and do not require a cast entry. For a no-form effect, the current scene must establish the subject manifesting or acting within that scene; a command attributed to it, a curse, an oath, an invocation or a mention alone does not establish a visible manifestation. Depiction rules permit how to show an established presence, never where to add one. Neighbor text can resolve identity or continuity of the current action, but cannot import an unrelated manifestation. Report an unsupported selected no-form effect as outside_instant, even when it obeys every depiction rule. An actual appearance or vision may be represented by permitted effects, including effects around an unoccupied seat for a seated metaphor. Ordinary illumination is still allowed. Check framing speakers independently; selecting a narrator does not move them inside an instruction or embedded story.
2. Simultaneity: compare each character AND each handled object's state across primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Treat every clause as describing this one image, not as a sequence an image model can choose between. An object held above a bench cannot also have been put down on it; walking up cannot also be kneeling. This applies to incidental people and props without cast IDs too. A hand touching an object already resting on a bench is compatible; holding an object while looking at it is compatible. Do not reject ordinary simultaneous gestures or infer a sequence from a conjunction alone. For not_one_instant, cite one exact conflicting phrase in planQuote and name the other conflicting phrase in the reason.
For each problem, copy planQuote: a short exact phrase from the scene fields, or a selected id, that shows it. Give a one-sentence reason. Judge only the plan against the moment; do not suggest a new plan.

DEPICTION RULES
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.

Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return. People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples. Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor. Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.

You are the scene planner of an illustration engine. You get one moment of a work's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work brief's tone and depiction rules, the era, the section look, and the cast on stage in the section. Plan one single scene that depicts this moment. Return only JSON.
Rules: single scene, no collage. Choose which of the listed cast are present in this moment and provide each once in `selectedCast` with its id and source evidence; leave out cast who are elsewhere in the section. Keep every depiction rule. Do not describe anyone's fixed appearance (canon does that) and do not name an art style or rendering technique; describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Each field is one or two short phrases, at most 220 characters. No text or written elements in the scene.
Establish presence from the scene being illustrated. A shared wardrobe, a narrator's viewpoint or a neighboring mention alone does not establish presence. Neighbors may resolve identity and continuity in the current scene; do not import cast from a separate adjacent event. The section cast and look cover multiple moments, not a roster to depict in every image. Apply shared clothing and props only to selected entries. Every cast entry described in any scene field must be selected in `selectedCast`; never describe an available cast member without selecting it. People, crowds, roles and animals with no cast entry may be described by role and situation when the moment needs them; they receive no fixed appearance and are never given a recurring character's name.
Identify the action the moment depicts before selecting cast. If it is inside a narrated story, parable, dream, vision or recollection, depict that scene's actors and setting. Do not place its framing speaker, listener or narrator inside it unless the text establishes their participation there. Reporting "I saw" supplies a viewpoint, not a visible observer. Shared look details from the framing scene do not establish the inner scene's cast or place.
Choose the scene before applying the shared look. In `grounding.focusQuote`, copy a short exact clause from MOMENT for the action or state to illustrate. If the moment recounts multiple actions, choose one representative instant; do not illustrate all steps. A character cannot occupy successive poses or places at once. Using the cast evidence, state that instant once in `grounding.instant`: where each selected formed character is and their one pose or movement, and the state or placement of selected places, objects and no-form effects (an effect's placement, never a bodily pose, seated presence or denied figure). Then write every scene field from that sentence, repeating its poses and places and adding no earlier or later step; for example, someone still walking toward a door cannot also be seated at the table. Keep each handled object in one state too: holding an object above a surface and putting it down are different instants. Choose one and keep its support, contact and placement consistent in primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Describe the chosen state rather than an action followed by its result. Ordinary simultaneous gestures, such as looking at an object while holding it, are allowed. Set `grounding.singleInstant` false if the fields cannot match it.
Select each participating entry exactly once in `selectedCast`, with its entryId and exact words from MOMENT anchoring its participation at that instant. This is the only selection list: there is no separate present list or grounding.cast. Put section cast you considered and left out in `consideredCast`, classified as framing, mentioned, separate_event or uncertain; use an empty list when there are none. Such records select no one, and an entry cannot appear in both lists. Every quote copies its source exactly; to skip words, give exact fragments in source order separated by an ellipsis (…), never paraphrased or reordered. Only selectedCast entries may be rendered; select only participants in the chosen instant. Do not select framing, merely mentioned, separate-event or uncertain entries. A first-person report of seeing or telling is framing evidence, not evidence of visible participation. Cast introduced in a later event remain absent from the chosen instant even if the shared look describes their clothes. A neighbor may resolve a current pronoun, ownership or continuing location, but cannot supply presence missing from MOMENT. Copy any needed neighbor evidence separately, with contextSource previous or next; otherwise use none and an empty contextQuote. Include locations, objects and permitted no-form presences in this evidence, not only people. A selected location or object that continues from a neighbor may leave its MOMENT quote empty and be anchored by an exact quote from that neighbor alone; characters and groups always need words from MOMENT. These evidence quotes are audit data, never scene prose. Apply the section look only after choosing this instant and its participants.
Report `missingCast` when the moment requires a named character or group whom the story follows beyond this moment, so its look must stay consistent across images, and it has no cast entry; this applies to secondary characters as well as the main actor. Never report a role, a generic crowd or an animal, a person named only in passing (for example in a list), or anyone in the available cast: describe those without canon instead. A recurring named group is not a generic crowd, even when it appears as one. If an available cast member's presence is uncertain, choose an instant the text establishes rather than reporting it missing. A moment without an event (a list, law, saying or greeting) still gets a scene that illustrates its content or setting. Do not replace a missing named character with a framing figure or omit that character to fit the list. When `missingCast` is nonempty, return empty `selectedCast` and `consideredCast`, empty `grounding.focusQuote` and `grounding.instant`, and empty scene fields; preparation will stop for a source correction. Otherwise return an empty `missingCast` list. This is a report of missing required canon, not a request to create it.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return. People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples. Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor. Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.
STORY SECTION: Solomon's building projects and ships

MOMENT (2 Chronicles 8:11): Solomon brought up Pharaoh’s daughter out of David’s city to the house that he had built for her; for he said, “My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because the places where Yahweh’s ark has come are holy.”
PREVIOUS: These were the chief officers of King Solomon, even two-hundred fifty, who ruled over the people.
NEXT: Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to Yahweh on Yahweh’s altar which he had built before the porch,

SECTION LOOK (shared conditions; not evidence of moment presence): place: Jerusalem: royal palace precincts, stone walls and cedar-beamed halls, with the temple courts nearby, and a Phoenician-style harbor port at Ezion-geber; time: Bright daytime, shifting to the warm glow of evening; weather: Clear, dry sky with a light desert breeze; light: Strong golden Levantine sunlight with soft shadows in stone courtyards; clothing: Tunics, cloaks and court robes of linen and wool; period armor for guards; priestly linen near the temple

momentQuote.description: Exact words from MOMENT establishing this entry's participation or physical presence at the chosen instant. A pronoun or continuing setting is valid with context support; a narrator's report alone is not participation.

contextSource.description: Use a neighbor only to resolve the identity or continuity of participation already anchored in momentQuote, never to add another event's participants.

contextQuote.description: Exact words from the named neighbor supporting identity or continuity; empty when contextSource is none.

primarySubject.description: The main subject at the chosen instant, in the pose and place stated in grounding.instant.

action.description: What happens at that one instant, matching grounding.instant; no earlier or later step.

setting.description: The physical place and surroundings of this single scene, consistent with the section look and era.

secondaryElements.description: Supporting selected cast, props and details with their placement at the same instant.

mood.description: The emotional atmosphere of this moment.

timeOfDay.description: This moment's time of day and situational illumination, consistent with the section look.

composition.description: Viewpoint, framing and relative placement of that same instant, introducing no other pose. Independent of art style and rendering technique.

missingCast.description: Named characters or groups the story follows beyond this moment, required here and absent from the available section cast. Include such actors inside embedded stories or visions. Never roles, crowds, animals, people named only in passing, or entries already in the cast. Usually empty; never invent canon or substitute framing figures.

A recurring named group is not a generic crowd, even when it appears as one. Do not replace a missing named character with a framing figure or omit that character to fit the list.
